meta.note: Original EnglishFarm learning content. Topic progression is informed by the organisation and level progression of the user-provided English Vocabulary in Use series; wording, examples, readings and tasks are newly written for the game.
meta.vocabulary_rotation: Each game-level pool contains 9 words, giving three non-overlapping Learn sessions before cycling.
meta.writing_note: Task 1 and Task 2 are VSTEP-style adaptations for gameplay. The uploaded Vocabulary in Use archive does not contain a VSTEP writing template source.

vocabulary: Momo makes tea in the kitchen.
The bedroom is next to the bathroom.
Open the window in the morning.

reading.title: A Morning at Home
reading.passage: Momo lives in a small house near the farm. Every morning, Momo opens the window, makes breakfast in the kitchen and feeds the cat. Momo's cousin sometimes visits after school. They clean the table together before they go outside.

questions.prompt: Momo lives near the farm.
Momo makes breakfast in the ____.
Who sometimes visits Momo after school?

task1.title: Friendly message
task1.prompt: Write a short message to your cousin. Invite them to visit your home and say what you can do together.
template: I want to invite you to ...

vocabulary: I usually drink tea in the morning.
Emma gets up early on weekdays.

reading.title: A Busy Day
reading.passage: Momo usually gets up early and eats breakfast before going to the garden. At noon, Momo has lunch with Tom. In the evening, Momo washes vegetables and cooks dinner. After dinner, Momo drinks water because gardening can make people thirsty.

questions.prompt: Momo eats breakfast after going to the garden.
At noon, Momo has lunch with ____.
Why does Momo drink water after dinner?
answers: because gardening can make people thirsty

task1.title: Daily routine
task1.prompt: Write to Emma about your daily routine. Mention when you get up, what you eat and one thing you do in the evening.

vocabulary: The price is on the sign.
Keep the receipt after you pay.
There is a short queue at the shop.

reading.title: At Mia's Market
reading.passage: Mia's market is busy on Saturday mornings. Customers compare prices before they buy fruit and vegetables. One customer pays in cash and asks for a receipt. The carrots are cheaper than the apples today, so the customer buys two bags of carrots.

questions.prompt: Match the person to the action: Who asks for a receipt?
The apples are cheaper than the carrots.
The customer buys two bags of ____.

task1.title: Shopping email
task1.prompt: Write an email to Mia asking about the price of two products and whether you can pay in cash.
template: I am writing to ask about ...
I would also like to know ...

vocabulary: Keep your ticket until the end of the journey.

reading.title: A Short Trip
reading.passage: Momo books a room before travelling to a nearby town. The bus should leave at eight, but there is a thirty-minute delay. Momo uses a map to find the hotel after arriving at the station. The luggage is light, so walking to the hotel is easy.

questions.prompt: The bus has a ____-minute delay.
What helps Momo find the hotel?
Why is walking to the hotel easy?

task1.title: Travel message
task1.prompt: Write to a friend about a short trip. Say when you leave, how you travel and where you will stay.

reading.title: Learning Online
reading.passage: Lily gives Momo a short lesson about studying English online. She says a dictionary can help with new words, but learners should also read examples. Momo writes new words in a notebook and sends Lily an email with two questions. Lily replies that regular practice is more important than avoiding every mistake.

questions.prompt: Lily says learners should only use a dictionary.
Momo sends Lily an ____ with two questions.
What does Lily say is more important than avoiding every mistake?

task1.title: Study email
task1.prompt: Write an email to Lily asking for advice on improving your English. Mention one problem and one thing you already do to practise.

reading.title: A New Study Plan
reading.passage: Momo has been missing deadlines because farm work often changes the daily schedule. Lily suggests dividing large assignments into smaller tasks and reviewing progress every evening. Momo agrees to try the plan for two weeks and asks Lily for feedback at the end of the trial.

questions.prompt: Momo has never missed a deadline.
Who suggests dividing assignments into smaller tasks?
How long will Momo try the new plan?

task1.title: Advice email
task1.prompt: Write an email to Lily about a problem with your study schedule. Explain the problem, describe what you have tried and ask for advice.
template: I'm writing to ask for advice about ...

task2.title: Opinion paragraph
task2.prompt: Some learners prefer studying alone, while others prefer studying with friends. Give your opinion and support it with reasons and examples.

reading.title: Changing a Routine
reading.passage: After several weeks of feeling tired, Tom decides to change his routine. He goes to bed earlier, eats a more balanced breakfast and takes short walks instead of working through every break. After a month, he has more energy and feels less stressed, although he still has busy days.

questions.prompt: Tom completely stops having busy days.
Tom takes short ____ instead of working through every break.
What two improvements does Tom notice after a month?
answers: he has more energy and feels less stressed

task1.title: Health advice letter
task1.prompt: Write to a friend who often feels tired. Suggest two realistic lifestyle changes and explain why they may help.

task2.title: Discussion essay
task2.prompt: Some people think schools should teach students more about healthy lifestyles. Discuss this view and give your opinion.

reading.title: A Digital Booking System
reading.passage: Mia introduces an online booking system so customers can reserve produce before market day. She believes the system will reduce queues and help the farm plan deliveries more efficiently. However, some customers are concerned about privacy and prefer to order in person. Mia decides to keep both options during a three-month trial.

questions.prompt: Mia believes the online system will make planning more efficient.
All customers prefer online booking.
How long will Mia keep both ordering options during the trial?

task1.title: Formal email
task1.prompt: Write a formal email to Mia giving feedback on the new booking system. Mention one advantage, one concern and one suggestion.
template: I am writing to provide feedback on ...

task2.title: Advantages and disadvantages essay
task2.prompt: Online services are replacing face-to-face services in many areas of daily life. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages.

reading.title: The Town Recycling Plan
reading.passage: The town council proposes a recycling plan that would require households to separate paper, glass and food waste. Supporters argue that the policy could reduce landfill use and raise environmental awareness. Critics agree with the goal but worry that the collection schedule may be inconvenient for older residents. The council plans to test the system in two neighbourhoods before expanding it.

questions.prompt: Supporters believe the plan could reduce landfill use.
Who worries about the collection schedule?
The council will first test the system in two ____.

task1.title: Letter to the council
task1.prompt: Write a formal letter to the town council about the recycling plan. State your position, identify one practical concern and suggest a solution.

task2.title: Problem–solution essay
task2.prompt: Many towns are producing more household waste than before. What problems does this create, and what solutions could local authorities introduce?

vocabulary: The headline attracted a lot of attention.

reading.title: Checking a Viral Story
reading.passage: A story about a new farming law spreads quickly on social media. The headline is dramatic, but the article does not link to the original policy document. Emma checks the council website and discovers that the law has not yet been approved. She posts a correction and explains why readers should verify claims before sharing them.

questions.prompt: Emma thinks readers should verify claims before sharing them.
The farming law has already been approved.
Where does Emma check the information?

task1.title: Correction email
task1.prompt: Write an email to a community group correcting a misleading story. Explain what was inaccurate, give the verified information and advise readers what to do next.

task2.title: Opinion essay
task2.prompt: People increasingly get news from social media rather than traditional news organisations. To what extent is this a positive development?

reading.title: Evaluating a Training Programme
reading.passage: A cooperative introduces a six-week training programme designed to improve staff communication. The initial survey suggests higher confidence, but the evaluators caution that self-reported confidence is not equivalent to measurable performance. They recommend combining surveys with observed tasks and follow-up interviews before deciding whether the programme should be expanded.

questions.prompt: The evaluators consider self-reported confidence sufficient evidence of improved performance.
Which method is suggested in addition to surveys?
What decision will the extra evidence help inform?
answers: whether the programme should be expanded

task1.title: Professional recommendation
task1.prompt: Write a formal email to the cooperative manager recommending how the training programme should be evaluated before expansion.

task2.title: Critical discussion essay
task2.prompt: Organisations often evaluate training using participants' satisfaction rather than long-term performance. Discuss the limitations of this approach and propose a more rigorous alternative.

reading.title: Resolving a Team Conflict
reading.passage: Two members of the market team disagree about how customer complaints should be handled. What begins as a procedural dispute becomes personal because each interprets the other's short messages as dismissive. Clara asks them to meet face to face, identify the underlying concerns and agree on a shared response policy. The meeting does not remove every disagreement, but it restores enough trust for the team to continue working effectively.

questions.prompt: Clara believes the conflict is purely personal.
The disagreement began as a ____ dispute.
What does the meeting restore?
answers: enough trust for the team to continue working effectively

task1.title: Mediation email
task1.prompt: Write a tactful email to two colleagues after a disagreement. Summarise the shared concern, suggest a compromise and propose a next step.
template: It seems the central issue is ...

task2.title: Argument essay
task2.prompt: Some people argue that workplace conflict is beneficial because it encourages better decisions. Others believe it mainly damages cooperation. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

reading.title: Automated Recommendations
reading.passage: A local platform begins using an algorithm to recommend news and community notices. Although engagement rises, researchers warn that the system may repeatedly show users material similar to what they already prefer. The platform responds by publishing a transparency note and adding controls that allow users to adjust recommendation settings. Critics welcome the change but argue that independent auditing is still necessary.

questions.prompt: Researchers believe higher engagement proves the recommendation system is beneficial.
What does the platform add for users?
What additional measure do critics still want?

task1.title: Policy feedback
task1.prompt: Write a formal response to the platform. Evaluate the transparency measures and recommend one additional safeguard.

task2.title: Discursive essay
task2.prompt: Recommendation algorithms make information more convenient but may narrow what users see. Discuss the extent to which platforms should be responsible for preventing this effect.

reading.title: Restricting Delivery Traffic
reading.passage: The town is considering restrictions on delivery vehicles in the central market district. Supporters expect cleaner air and safer streets, while small businesses argue that fixed delivery windows could raise costs and reduce flexibility. A pilot scheme would exempt low-emission vehicles and provide shared loading areas. Whether the policy succeeds will depend less on the headline restriction than on how exemptions, enforcement and infrastructure are implemented.

questions.prompt: The writer suggests implementation details may be more important than the headline restriction.
All delivery vehicles would be completely banned under the pilot scheme.
Name one feature of the pilot scheme designed to reduce the burden on businesses.

task1.title: Consultation response
task1.prompt: Write a formal consultation response on the proposed delivery restrictions. Acknowledge the environmental objective, assess the burden on small businesses and recommend implementation safeguards.

task2.title: Policy evaluation essay
task2.prompt: Environmental policies often impose short-term costs on individuals or businesses. To what extent should governments accept these costs in pursuit of long-term public benefits?

reading.title: Interpreting Limited Evidence
reading.passage: A small pilot study reports that learners who used a game-based vocabulary tool remembered more words after one week than learners who used a conventional list. The result is promising, but the groups were not randomly assigned and the study did not measure retention after several months. The authors therefore describe the findings as preliminary and call for larger controlled studies before making broad claims about effectiveness.

questions.prompt: The authors believe the pilot study proves long-term superiority of game-based learning.
The groups were not randomly ____.
Why do the authors call for larger controlled studies?
answers: before making broad claims about effectiveness
to make broader claims about effectiveness
because the current findings are preliminary

task1.title: Academic-style summary email
task1.prompt: Write to a project supervisor summarising the study's main finding, two limitations and an appropriate next research step.

task2.title: Evidence-based essay
task2.prompt: Educational technology should be adopted only when strong evidence shows that it improves learning outcomes. Critically evaluate this statement.
template: Reasons controlled experimentation may be difficult
